title: One database per wallet: record the wallet on every trade, or lock the database file, or refuse a database owned by another wallet

options.name: Keep current behaviour (no wallet on rows, no file lock)
options.risk: Two bots with different wallets on one file mark each other's positions failed on restart and share every risk total (AUD-DB-015).

options.name: Store the owning wallet address in the database and refuse to start with a different wallet
options.behavior_impact: A second wallet cannot use the file at all.
options.risk: Small schema addition; the operator must create a separate database for a second wallet.

options.name: Add a wallet column to trades and scope every query by the running wallet
options.behavior_impact: Several wallets can share one file safely.
options.risk: Touches every query on the money path; a larger migration.

options.name: A second process lock keyed by the canonical DB path (beside the 22-13 wallet lock)
options.behavior_impact: Only one bot process of any wallet can use the file.
options.risk: Scripts that open the DB while the bot runs (preflight, pause, resume) must use the try-acquire query or read-only opens.

recommendation: owner-check: the bot is single-wallet by design, so refusing a foreign wallet is the smallest safe change.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract); S2, the setup is not used today.
behavior_impact: Decides whether a database can be shared across wallets.
needed_by: Phase 24 discussion (with the 22-13 lock re-audit in 22-29)
